$comment: Copy this file to the ROOT of each project you work in and rename it to 'sovai.config.json', then edit the three path lists to match that project's actual layout and record where this project's tickets go. SoVai's hooks walk up from an edited file to the nearest sovai.config.json to decide what the file is; a project with no config is NOT gated at all. Only this project knows which of its directories are UI, and ADR-0007 makes that distinction load-bearing, which is why there is no plugin-side default to fall back on. Keys: 'productionLogic' = paths where TDD is mandatory (a first edit there points at the `tdd` skill, and ending the session without invoking it is blocked); 'ui' = the deliberate TDD exception, tested after implementation via `ui-testing`; 'tests' = test files, gated by nothing. Precedence is tests, then ui, then productionLogic — so UI paths nested under a production path win, and you never write exclusions into productionLogic. Patterns are shell globs matched against the path relative to this file's directory, where '*' also crosses '/': 'src/**' matches 'src/a/b.ts', and '*.test.*' matches a test file at any depth. Prefer that forgiving form over '**/*.test.*', which requires at least one directory and so misses a test file at the project root. 'tracker' tells `to-tickets` and `wrap-up` where issues are published: 'kind' is one of the trackers described in the to-tickets skill's TRACKERS.md ('local' writes markdown files into the effort's own directory and always works), and the remaining fields are whatever that tracker needs to identify a destination — 'team'/'project' for Linear, 'project' for Jira, 'repo' for GitHub. 'phasesAsParents' says whether to hang each ticket off a parent issue representing its phase. There is NO default tracker: with this key absent, to-tickets asks once and offers to write the answer here, and falls to local markdown when nobody is around to ask. Unlike the three path lists, this key is read by skills rather than by the hooks.
